## Why the apply stopped (both recorded in `D-P35.1a-1`)

1. **Missing job-class runtime identities.** The committed
   `ops/gcp/scheduled-ops.sh` deploys `sig-probe` onto `sig-probe-rt@…` and
   the whole ingest fleet + `sig-replay-ingest` onto `sig-ingest-rt@…` —
   identities created by `ops/gcp/iam-job-identities.sh`, **P34.42b's
   still-queued leg** (its S5-3 OM-20 pre-authorisation expired at
   GATE-G4). `pre/service-accounts.json` shows only the default compute
   SA + `sig-scheduler` + the three P34.42a service SAs; all 88 live jobs
   run as the compute SA. The apply's first `run jobs deploy` would be
   refused for a nonexistent service account — and deploying onto any
   substituted identity would silently do or undo another leg's scoped
   mutation.
2. **The declared trigger set outgrew the authorised command.** Since the
   leg queued on 2026-10-10 (then: exactly two missing triggers),
   `ops/cadence.toml` gained the ten `r11-*` wave batches and the two
   tribal screened-lane rows — each annotated *"created `--paused`
   (R6)"*. The verbatim plain `--apply` this leg is authorised for would
   create them **ENABLED**, contradicting the declared first-run protocol
   and encroaching on P35.11's wave legs (ING-GO-A / OP-26).

The decision routed to **`D-P35.1a-1` (OPEN)**: (a) re-authorise + run
P34.42b's jobs-IAM leg first, then re-run this leg on
`r11/P35.1a-live-2`, with the operator naming how the new wave
declarations reconcile (`--paused` variant or their own legs); or
(b) re-split the leg so only the scheduler-of-record half deploys.
